title: QBR relationship health runbook and signals log
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, facilitator-first runbook for Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) that centers relationship health rather than metrics alone. It includes a short agenda, a facilitation script with suggested phrasing, a pre-meeting prep checklist, and a compact "renewal signal" tracker you can fill in during or right after the meeting. Built for 45–60 minute customer QBRs where renewal is 6–12 months out and the account team needs a consistent, repeatable way to identify risk and next actions.

When to use this doc:
- Standard QBR for mid-market and enterprise customers (renewal 6–12 months)
- When you want a rapid indicator of churn risk during the meeting
- When product/engineering presence is optional (invite only if there are clear technical escalations)

Meeting length options (pick one):
- 30 min (status + top 2 items)
- 45 min (recommended for most renewals)
- 60 min (strategic customers, multiple stakeholders)

Suggested 45-min agenda (timeboxed):
1) Quick opening & goals (5 min) — facilitator
  - "Thanks for your time — today we want to run through health, top wins/blocks, and agree next steps tied to your renewal goals."
2) Customer perspective (10 min) — ask the champion to lead
  - Prompts: "What's gone well? What would you change if you had a magic wand?"
3) Usage & outcomes highlight (8 min) — CSM + data snapshot
  - Bring 2 slides (or console view): adoption trend, latency/cost surprises, key outcomes tied to business metrics
  - Call out any recent incidents and remediation status
4) Open issues & risk map (12 min) — collaborative (facilitator/solutions)
  - Use the renewal signal tracker (see below) to mark concern levels in real time
  - If technical risk > medium, propose follow-up with engineering within 48 hours
5) Commercial & roadmap alignment (6 min) — commercial owner + product/PM notes
  - Surface contract timeline, any pending procurement items, pricing questions, and product features that matter for the renewal
6) Summarize actions & close (4 min) — facilitator
  - Confirm owners, deadlines, and date for next checkpoint

Facilitation script (snippets you can copy/paste)
- Opening: "Hi everyone — quick agenda: hear your perspective, show a snapshot of how things are trending, call out any blockers, and agree on the most important next steps. Is that good? Any additional items to add?"
- When customer hesitates: "Totally understand — can you share the top 1–2 outcomes you need this quarter so we can prioritize?"
- When a technical issue surfaces: "Thank you for flagging that. We will schedule a technical deep-dive and include engineering — does 48–72 hours work for you?"
- When procurement delay appears: "Can you share the procurement timeline and any gating stakeholders? We’ll escalate internally to help unblock."

Pre-meeting checklist (what the CSM does 48–72 hours before):
- Send agenda + goals, list of attendees, and ask for any additional topics (template email available in Confluence)
- Run data snapshot: 90/30/7-day usage, error rates, latency percentiles, cost delta vs. forecast
- Pre-score renewal signals (low/medium/high) based on objective data + recent conversations
- Confirm internal attendees: solutions_engineer? product PM? account exec?
- Prep 2–3 slides: (1) customer outcomes + adoption, (2) open issues & roadmap asks

Renewal signal tracker (quick taxonomy + examples)
- Executive alignment (Low/Medium/High) — examples: executive sponsor active in strategic planning = Low; sponsor changed = High
- Product fit & adoption (Low/Medium/High) — examples: expanding ARR and regular usage = Low; plateauing usage and feature gaps = Medium/High
- Technical stability (Low/Medium/High) — examples: no incidents last 90 days = Low; repeated P1s or unresolved performance regressions = High
- Commercial friction (Low/Medium/High) — examples: contract renewal paused for budget = High; contract discussions underway with known timeline = Medium
- Support & CS experience (Low/Medium/High) — examples: positive NPS/CSAT follow-ups = Low; repeated case reopenings or slow RT = Medium/High

How to use the tracker during the meeting:
- One person (typically facilitator) updates a single row per signal with Low/Medium/High and short rationale (1–2 bullets).
- Assign an "owner" for each High signal with a required next step within 7 business days.
- If more than two High signals: escalate to AE + CSM manager for a risk playbook within 48 hours.

Sample scoring rubric (0–3) for quick quantification (optional):
- 0 = No signal / green; 1 = minor concern; 2 = moderate risk; 3 = severe risk (high probability of non-renewal if not mitigated)
- Use rubric post-meeting to compute a composite score for internal triage (sum of signal scores). Set internal thresholds: 0–3 = healthy, 4–6 = watch, 7+ = urgent

Note capture template (fill during or immediately after meeting):
- Customer: {{customer_name}}
- Date: {{date}}
- Attendees: {{names + titles}}
- Highlights (wins/outcomes):
  - 1)
  - 2)
- Open issues & owners (include ETA):
  - Issue A — owner — ETA
  - Issue B — owner — ETA
- Renewal signals (exec alignment, adoption, technical, commercial, support):
  - Exec alignment: [Low/Medium/High] — note
  - Adoption: [Low/Medium/High] — note
  - Tech: [Low/Medium/High] — note
  - Commercial: [Low/Medium/High] — note
  - Support: [Low/Medium/High] — note
- Agreed next steps & owners (3 items max):
  1)
  2)
  3)
- Target date for check-in: {{date}}

Post-meeting follow-ups (timeline):
- Within 24 hours: send meeting notes and action list to attendees (CS to send)
- Within 48–72 hours: schedule technical deep-dive if Tech signal >= Medium and unresolved
- Within 7 business days: owner updates status in the renewal tracker and pings AE if commercial friction present
- Weekly until resolved: short status sync until all High signals are closed

Escalation playbook (triggered when composite score >= 7 or more than two High signals):
- Immediately: AE + CSM manager join a triage call (30 min) to create a 14-day remediation plan - Assign a product/engineering liaison and set SLAs for bug fixes or mitigations
- If unresolved after 14 days: prepare executive briefing for customer execs and Redwood leadership as needed

Templates & artifacts to reuse (internal links):
- Email invite + agenda template: confluence:CS/qbr-templates/email-invite
- Data extraction script for usage snapshot: github:internal/cs-scripts/usage-snapshot
- Risk playbook checklist: confluence:CS/risk-playbook

Notes / open questions (working):
- Should we surface a short standardized health score in the QBR slide deck (Y/N)? Draft: composite rubric + one-line rationale.
- Consider an optional 15-min "exec only" follow-up for customers with High exec risk.
- Need a short training checklist for new CSMs to run this runbook (bootcamp inclusion).

Quick wins to adopt immediately:
- Always send the pre-read 48 hours before — even if short — Pre-populate the renewal signal tracker with objective metrics so discussion is focused on interpretation, not data collection

History: created as a distilled, facilitator-friendly iteration after several long-format QBRs where teams had inconsistent risk signals. Intention: keep meetings action-oriented and make renewal risk visible in the meeting so internal follow-ups are faster.

-- end of runbook --
